verdict.rationale: Thoropass is a compliance SaaS platform, not an agent, so publishing an official MCP server is a fair question for it. A first-party help article, titled "Connecting to the Thoropass MCP server," documents a Thoropass MCP server. It lets an AI assistant work inside the workspace within limits the user sets, with tools to list audits and evidence requests and to add comments, attachments, and status updates. A probe confirms the documentation page exists. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of a working agent connection, and detailed setup/auth specifics in the evidence.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: The Thoropass MCP server lets your AI assistant help with that work right where you're already working, so you don't have to export data and upload it somewhere else.
MCP lets the assistant work directly inside your Thoropass workspace, within limits you set.
List audits and view audit details ... List evidence requests, view their details, and see the systems tied to them
Add comments, attachments, and status updates to evidence requests
